summary: A Gainesville Times article (only its headline and opening text were readable) and a photo caption dated 3 Jan 2019 describe the Lula tower as 100 ft high, beside the GFC office and one of few still in use; its history and current status are unverified.

evidence.supports: Tower at Lula in Hall County at the listed coordinates, with codes BLL-64456, usgs and gfc-915
Tower reaches 100 feet (about 30.5 m), stands next to the Georgia Forestry Commission office in Lula, and is one of few still in use around Georgia
evidence.quote: Reaching 100 feet high, the fire tower next to the Georgia Forestry Commission office in Lula is one of few still in use around Georgia.

evidence.supports: Photo caption dated Thursday, January 3, 2019, showing the tower at the Georgia Forestry Commission in Lula
evidence.quote: Doug Andrews, chief ranger with the Georgia Forestry Commission, stands in front of a fire tower at the Georgia Forestry Commission in Lula on Thursday, Jan. 3, 2019.

evidence.supports: Photo caption: the tower reaches 100 feet and is one of the few still in use around Georgia
evidence.quote: The fire tower reaches 100 feet high and is one of the few still in use around Georgia.

evidence.supports: Article headline: the Lula fire tower has survived decades of demolition
evidence.quote: Dodging decades of demolition: How the Lula fire tower has survived

sources.title: Dodging decades of demolition: How the Lula fire tower has survived

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The Gainesville Times page returned only about 617 characters (headline, a photo caption and the opening text), so the article's own publication date and its account of the demolition threats were not read; the story says only what the headline and opening text support, and dates only the photo caption (3 Jan 2019). Height 100 ft is converted to 30.5 m. The tnlandforms row also carries a usgs tag (BLL-64456 usgs gfc-915) that the record omits. The article photo by Austin Steele (January 2019) exists, but no image URL was retrieved, so there is no photos entry. Unverified lead, NOT cited: search results list a Hall County Forester office at 5707 Lula Road, which may help check access. Current status and public access are unknown after 2019. Confidence is medium for location and height, low for history. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the article date '2019' was unsupported and was replaced with the caption date; the caption's 100 ft and still-in-use sentence was added as its own quote.
